messages.subject: Ok I am new at this so be nice - Help with this error: initial model-implied matrix (Sigma) is not positive definite;   check your model and/or starting parameters in group 2.
parts:
I am running a group invariance test for a measurement model: 

MITcon_SRO_W3 <- '


NV =~ NA* NV1 + NV2 + NV3 + NV4 + NV5 + NV6 + NV7 + NV8 + NV9 + NV10 + NV11 + NV12 + NV13 + NV15 + NV16 + NV17 + NV18 + NV19 + NV20 + NV21


VO =~ NA * VO1 + VO2 + VO3 + VO4 + VO5 + VO6 + VO7 + VO8 + VO9 + VO10 + VO11


NV ~~ 1* NV

VO ~~ 1* VO'


fitMITcon_SRO_W3 <- cfa(MITcon_SRO_W3, data = ProjectData, missing = "fiml", group = "HI_Bi_B21")



But I am getting this error "lavaan ERROR: initial model-implied matrix (Sigma) is not positive definite;

  check your model and/or starting parameters in group 2." The model converges just fine until I add the grouping variable. 


I recently learned what a reprex Is, but I am not sure how to share my data?


Any help would be amazing

messages.subject: Re: Ok I am new at this so be nice - Help with this error: initial model-implied matrix (Sigma) is not positive definite;   check your model and/or starting parameters in group 2.
parts:
Without saying anything about your lavaan syntax, the situation you describe is not uncommon.
A model can work without group distinctions. But when you split your data into 2 groups--usually on a naturally occurring variable--for one group the model has a covariance matrix that is not identified.
This usually means the correlation between the 2 factors for that one group is >1.00 or very close to it.
In other words you have specified a distinction that cannot be fitted to that group's data.

Possible causes can include:
  • the offending group sample size is too small relative to the number of variables
  • the offending group is from a different population than the other
  • your model is wrong
good luck in trouble-shooting causes of non-invariance between these two groups.

messages.subject: Re: Ok I am new at this so be nice - Help with this error: initial model-implied matrix (Sigma) is not positive definite;   check your model and/or starting parameters in group 2.
parts:
Brandon
that would remove the covariance problem but you may find that the model has poor fit because you are setting as zero the covariance between the 2 factors.
just as easily you could test it as 1 model.
the fit will not be the same.

otherwise, you could take the strategy of trimming the model by removing items that have strong between factor residual correlations. You might find items with strong modification indices which if you removed would make the covariance no longer not identified. However, that changes your model by removing items--you have plenty--but it changes the meaning of the factors.
